o.text: Inherited from Proto-Turkic *agrï-. Cognate with Turkish ağrımak (“to ache”), Crimean Tatar ağırmaq (“to become ill”).
From Turkish sopa. See more cases of initial /s/-voicing at Azerbaijani zəngin.

From Proto-Turkic *ürk- (“to be afraid”).
Cognate with
Old Uyghur [script needed] (ürk-, “to startle (of sheep)”);
Kyrgyz үркүү (ürküü, “to be frightened of”), Southern Altai ӱркӱӱр (ürküür), Uzbek hurkmoq, Uyghur ئۈركىمەك (ürkimek), Turkish ürkmek and etc.

From Proto-Turkic *yor(ɨ)- (“to walk”).
Cognate with Turkish yorga, Turkmen ýorga, Kazakh жорға (jorğa), Kyrgyz жорго (jorgo), Uzbek yoʻrgʻa, Bashkir юрға (yorğa), Yakut дьоруо (joruo).
